Binary 2D Segmentation

binary-segmentation.Rmd

This experimental contract remains unpromoted (vetted=FALSE) pending reviewer acceptance of the executed evidence. The pytorch_resnet18_segmentation contract fits a binary mask on the canonical 128 by 128 grid. Each custodian must select the patient privacy unit and configure its image and mask roots. The analyst supplies schema column names and asset aliases, never filesystem roots or privacy parameters.

The current evidence is protocol v5: public BUSI decoder pretraining followed by federated DP fine-tuning. Random-initialization v3 and v4 results remain separately labelled boundary evidence; v2 remains invalidated by its schedule defect. The September 20 reconciliation established that the previously packaged current files were stale v3 copies. The current files now contain the verified v5 results. Mechanism checks remain separately recorded; execution and a passed utility floor do not constitute reviewer acceptance.

Paired image and mask schema

A samples table declares a stable subject identifier, image_id, an image path (default relative_path), and the mask path column passed as target. PNG/JPEG images and single-channel PNG masks are supported. Declare mask_values as "0,255" or "0,1"; masks are never intensity normalized. An optional mask_empty_col explicitly declares empty annotations. Without this declaration, a missing annotation is invalid, rather than a background example.

For each subject, the node selects the lexicographically first canonical image ID (trimmed Unicode NFC). Masks for that image are unioned. Conflicting image paths for the same selected ID invalidate the subject instead of introducing an order-dependent tie. Invalid paths, images, masks or pairings become fixed safe tensors with zero loss validity. Those subjects remain in the sampling census; no completeness counts are released.

Direct samples tables use custodian options dsflower.image_data_root and dsflower.mask_data_root. Imaging resources use admitted dsImaging image and mask_root descriptors. Both routes enforce the same asset containment checks.

Submit the fixed spatial contract 

model <- ds.flower.model.pytorch_resnet18_segmentation(
  sample_id_col = "image_id",
  image_path_col = "relative_path",
  mask_empty_col = "mask_empty",
  mask_values = "0,255",
  batch_size = 8L,
  local_epochs = 1L,
  learning_rate = 0.001
)

fit <- ds.flower.fit(
  conns, symbol = "samples", target = "mask_path",
  model = model, task = "segmentation", data_kind = "image",
  rounds = 5L, output_dir = "segmentation-model"
)

ds.flower.model("pytorch_resnet18_segmentation"), ds.flower.recipe() and ds.flower.submit() use the same contract. The target is a mask path role, so do not supply class levels, target bounds or tabular feature columns.

The resident encoder is ResNet18 through layer2, pinned to ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1 and profile resnet18_layer2_128_v1. The full checkpoint SHA256 is f37072fd47e89c5e827621c5baffa7500819f7896bbacec160b1a16c560e07ec. Custodians provision these exact weights before training. Missing or mismatched weights fail preflight. The encoder is frozen, in evaluation mode, outside the released module; its BatchNorm statistics never learn from private images.

The default decoder has three convolutions (128 to 32, 32 to 16, 16 to 1), ReLU activations and nearest upsampling by 2 then 4, producing [1,128,128]. The loss mixes per-image mean BCE and smoothed Dice with alpha=0.5 and smoothing 1. alpha=1 is the declared BCE ablation. There is no batch-wide Dice, trainable encoder, mixed precision, or image augmentation in this first profile.

The constructor defaults to random initialization and the 41,537-parameter decoder="current". It also supports decoder="narrow" (9,521 parameters; convolution channels 128 to 8, 8 to 4, 4 to 1) and decoder="pointwise" (129 parameters). Selecting the narrow architecture does not load a public decoder checkpoint. The v5 benchmark used the narrow decoder with a BUSI-pretrained checkpoint applied by campaign-only tooling outside the trusted DP runner. That tooling replaced both the live decoder parameters and the initial arrays transmitted by Flower. The constructor has no public-checkpoint loading argument, so the example above does not reproduce the v5 initialization.

Local prediction and public evaluation 

probabilities <- ds.flower.predict(
  "segmentation-model", c("public/image-1.png", "public/image-2.png"),
  type = "prob"
)
masks <- ds.flower.predict(
  "segmentation-model", c("public/image-1.png", "public/image-2.png"),
  type = "response"
)
# Both arrays use [image, channel, row, column] = [2, 1, 128, 128].
# Responses threshold probabilities at >= 0.5.

Prediction verifies the decoder artifact and the frozen encoder checkpoint before opening image paths. It shares the node’s stored-pixel orientation, RGB conversion, bilinear 128 by 128 resize and ImageNet channel normalization. Invalid local images receive fixed zero features. Outputs use the canonical grid. To map a binary prediction back to the stored native image of height H and width W, threshold at 0.5 on the canonical grid first, then use nearest resampling with the following zero-based coordinate rule (exact ties choose the larger canonical index):

native[r, c] = canonical[min(127, floor((r + 0.5) * 128 / H)),
                         min(127, floor((c + 0.5) * 128 / W))]

This retains stored-pixel orientation, with no EXIF rotation, cropping or padding. It restores the coordinate grid, not detail discarded by resizing. For known dimensions from an authorized local image, the same rule in R is:

canonical <- masks[1L, 1L, , ]
native_rows <- pmin(128L, floor((2 * seq_len(native_height) - 1) *
                                128 / (2 * native_height)) + 1L)
native_cols <- pmin(128L, floor((2 * seq_len(native_width) - 1) *
                                128 / (2 * native_width)) + 1L)
native_mask <- canonical[native_rows, native_cols, drop = FALSE]

Use these indices explicitly: resize libraries may differ at exact tie pixels through floating-point coordinate accumulation. Declare and label any native-resolution secondary metric with this mapping. The primary benchmark metric remains on the canonical 128 by 128 grid.

Channel-B evaluation uses public or independently authorized analyst-local held-out subjects. Report mean subject Dice and IoU at threshold 0.5, and report foreground-positive and empty-mask strata separately. Both-empty Dice is 1; exactly one empty mask gives Dice 0. Neither images nor predictions are returned from a private node for evaluation.

Private ds.flower.validate(), holdout, cross-validation and private-score HPO are unsupported for this contract and fail public preflight. The local HPO callback API does not create a private segmentation scoring route. Any public benchmark utility claim must cite an executed subject-disjoint protocol, exact central twins and the recorded gate results; the constructor alone establishes no utility claim.

Public benchmark evidence

The current preregistered v5 campaign uses BrEaST and BUS-BRA with three DSLite sites, subject-disjoint 80/20 splits, three seeds, epsilon 1, 4 and 8, delta 1e-5, clipping 1 and separate nominal batch-size 16 and 64 arms. Protocol v5 fixes 128 by 128 inputs and selects the narrow decoder, 60 public pretraining epochs, batch16 and 20 rounds from three-seed BUS-BRA inner validation. Batch64 is the prespecified sensitivity arm. Fine-tuning uses three local epochs per round (60 total), round-local Adam at learning rate 0.001, and no augmentation or mixed precision. BUS-BRA also has the nested 192-subject, BCE-only and heterogeneous-site extensions. The released federated DP model is compared with pooled DP, pooled nonprivate and federated nonprivate twins using the same seed-specific public-pretrained decoder, effective tensors, loss, optimizer and subject splits. Nonprivate twins are public benchmark diagnostics outside the released contract. The trivial comparison selects the strongest of four fixed masks: empty, full, a centered disk of radius 32, and a centered 64 by 64 square.

Public pretraining used 780 BUSI images from the Arya Shah Kaggle mirror, version 1, attributed to Al-Dhabyani et al. (2020). It is a disclosed nonprivate stage outside fine-tuning’s DP accounting. BUSI has no patient mapping for this protocol and supplies no held-out utility claim; within-BUSI duplicates were retained and cross-dataset near-duplicate screening was not claimed. The mirror’s CC0 declaration is preserved as provenance. provenance/busi-v1/provenance.json, public-pretraining-manifest.json and public-pretraining/audit.json bind the dataset, preprocessing, encoder and seed-specific checkpoint digests. The dataset ZIP SHA256 is 7fffc86a517934da55021f66641d81383058d26a30adb0ffab3780ca7e52d57d; the pretraining audit SHA256 is d59334151e074de56afaaec81e92930ddaad8371f7f2665577096ce4ff7d9d57. Dataset and checkpoint tensors are not distributed with the package.

Selection excluded outer-test subjects, but confirmation reused previously inspected public outer splits. These results describe public benchmark confirmation after development, not an unseen clinical test. Repeated benchmark runs are separately recorded; their privacy budgets must not be portrayed as one non-composed private release. The model remains vetted=FALSE.

The tables below read campaign-status.json, breast-evidence.json and busbra-evidence.json in each arm directory under inst/extdata/campaign/segmentation/ at render time. Arms are reported separately; batch16 is the selected primary arm and batch64 is sensitivity, with no averaging across arms. Current protocol.md is byte-identical to protocol-v5.md, SHA256 28a713f8ffe6f7bb7b74e7d59d13d1be265d5738b43503c60e6581a67e0c5820. The frozen protocol, dataset release hashes, licence texts, subject-mapping audits and split hashes are archived alongside the evidence. The archival assembler validates the complete JSON schemas, captured accountant steps, effective tensors, released artifacts and twin provenance. Rendering checks the schema identity, contract and protocol hash again. An incomplete cohort cannot produce a completed-matrix summary. Execution status is separate from utility acceptance and reviewer promotion.

The earlier negative results remain in retained/v3/ and retained/v4/, each with its original protocol. V4 uses the same selected narrow decoder and 20-round schedule with random initialization; v3 uses the original decoder and ten rounds. The following comparison retains those distinctions. The reconciliation report and audit-results.json under reconciliation-v5-20260920/ document the stale-path correction. Independent forward scoring reproduced all six v5 batch16 full-cohort epsilon8 results; the captured initialization matched the public checkpoints. Batch64 was not independently forward-scored in that audit.

The shortfall used by the envelope is pooled nonprivate Dice minus federated DP Dice. Positive values indicate lower utility for the released model. Epsilon-envelope flags compare changes against seed dispersion; near-central flags identify unexpectedly close agreement under the preregistered small-cohort rule. An unflagged envelope does not establish privacy by itself. Failed utility floors remain failed and do not trigger changes to epsilon, delta, clipping, subject retention or the preregistered protocol. Foreground-positive results remain visible even when empty-mask performance changes the overall mean.
